description: the read-only MCP observer server and its tool manifest exist
the tool manifest declares read_only:true and every exposed tool has kind:read (no write tool)
command: jq -e '.read_only == true and ([.tools[].kind] | all(. == "read"))' platform/mcp-servers/northstar-observer.tools.json >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: over stdio the server lists exactly get_health, get_info, get_readiness — the complete read-only surface, no write tool
command: out=$(printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' | node platform/mcp-servers/northstar-observer.js 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'select(.id==2) | .result.tools[].name' | sort | tr '\n' ' '); [ "$out" = 'get_health get_info get_readiness ' ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: NEGATIVE: a write-shaped tools/call (restart) is rejected because no such tool exists in the interface — the observer boundary is structural, not a permission check
command: resp=$(printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":9,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"restart","arguments":{"service":"orders-api"}}}' | node platform/mcp-servers/northstar-observer.js 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'select(.id==9) | (.error.message // "OK")'); echo "$resp" | grep -qi 'unknown tool' && echo pass || echo fail

description: POSITIVE: get_readiness returns typed JSON with the endpoint and http_status fields (typed contract, not raw text the agent must parse)
command: resp=$(printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_readiness","arguments":{"service":"orders-api"}}}' | node platform/mcp-servers/northstar-observer.js 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'select(.id==3) | .result.content[0].text'); echo "$resp" | jq -e '.endpoint == "/readyz" and has("http_status")' >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: the Agent Run Ledger captured all three shootout approaches (cli, skill, mcp)
command: jq -e -s '([.[].approach] | unique | sort) == ["cli","mcp","skill"]' labs/m7/shootout.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: the shootout ledger captured all three approaches (cli, skill, mcp) — the comparison was actually run, not read about
command: L=labs/m7/shootout.jsonl; [ -f $L ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; jq -e -s '([.[].approach] | unique | sort) == ["cli","mcp","skill"]' $L >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo complete || echo incomplete
